forces.title: Increased adoption of AI and digital transformation in Irish healthcare
forces.description: Artificial intelligence and digital transformation are becoming crucial across Irish healthcare, including private hospital operations and patient care pathways. This trend is driven by continued investment from providers in technologies such as electronic health records (EHRs), remote monitoring, digital prescribing, and automation. The 'Ireland’s AI for Care Strategy 2026-2030' offers a strategic framework, facilitating further integration and growth for digital health solutions over the long term.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Software emerging as critical growth driver for MedTech
forces.description: The MedTech industry is experiencing a structural shift where software, particularly Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), is becoming a critical avenue for differentiation, growth, and patient impact. This is driven by the maturation of hardware categories and increasing price pressures, leading MedTech organizations to focus on digital solutions for new recurring revenue models, workflow integration, and advanced care models like remote monitoring and data-driven decision support. This represents a significant tailwind for the digital health sector.
forces.source_title: The future of delivering software as a medical device

forces.title: AI advances improve software development productivity in MedTech
forces.description: Advances in artificial intelligence are significantly enhancing software productivity, with organizations across industries reporting 30 to 70 percent gains in development efficiency. For the MedTech sector, this presents a major opportunity to accelerate the creation and deployment of Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), fostering innovation and reducing time-to-market. This efficiency gain acts as a strong upside driver for digital health companies, enabling faster feature development and innovation cycles while meeting evolving market demands.
forces.source_title: The future of delivering software as a medical device

forces.title: MedTech organizations struggle to deliver regulated SaMD at pace
forces.description: Despite accelerating ambition for software development, MedTech organizations are struggling to deliver regulated Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) at a pace commensurate with market demand. Unlike other industries that have adopted agile models, life sciences software development remains constrained by phased approaches, extensive testing, verification, and documentation required for regulatory and quality standards. These processes can extend timelines by 20 to 30 percent and increase development costs, hindering rapid innovation and market entry for digital health solutions.
forces.source_title: The future of delivering software as a medical device

viewpoints.title: AI and digital transformation increasingly important for Irish healthcare
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland expects AI and digital transformation to play an increasingly important role across Ireland's healthcare sector, particularly in private hospital operations and patient care pathways. Providers are actively investing in technologies like electronic health records (EHRs), remote monitoring, digital prescribing, and automation. The country's 'AI for Care Strategy 2026-2030' provides a supportive framework for future adoption, indicating a positive outlook for the integration of digital health solutions in the coming years.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Digital health and AI to be deeply embedded in Irish care delivery
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland anticipates that digital health technologies, artificial intelligence, and integrated care models will become increasingly embedded within healthcare delivery in Ireland. This outlook is supported by favorable demographics, continued government investment, and sustained private sector activity. The projected significant increase in demand for home care by 2040, driven by population ageing and a shift towards community-based care, necessitates advanced digital solutions to improve productivity and service quality across the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

demand_drivers.description: Ireland's ageing population, increased life expectancy, and rising incidence of chronic disease drive demand for all healthcare services, including those enabled and optimized by digital health technologies.

Healthcare policy increasingly prioritizes independent living and care closer to home, necessitating the expansion of home care and community-based models, which are heavily reliant on remote monitoring and data-driven care delivery.

Overall increasing demand for healthcare services, coupled with capacity constraints, creates an imperative for digital solutions to improve productivity, support service quality, and manage patient flows efficiently.

pnl_drivers.description: Investment in AI, EHRs, and automation is expected to enhance operational efficiency, streamline workflows, and optimize resource utilization, positively impacting the profitability and cost-effectiveness of healthcare providers.

Data-driven care delivery and digital tools contribute to better patient outcomes, increased patient satisfaction, and improved quality standards, potentially leading to higher revenue streams or improved competitive positioning.

new_opportunities.description: The ongoing need for investment in AI, EHRs, automation, and data-driven care delivery across nursing homes, disability services, homecare, and private hospitals presents significant opportunities to modernize and expand healthcare infrastructure and services.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of expected investment in artificial intelligence, electronic health records (EHRs), automation, and data-driven care delivery to improve productivity and support service quality in Ireland. No explicit market size or CAGR provided, but strong underlying demand drivers identified for digital health technologies.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

demand_drivers.description: As traditional MedTech hardware markets mature and face increasing price pressure, software emerges as a crucial avenue for differentiation, growth, and patient impact.
Software enables new recurring revenue streams, such as premium analytics layers and subscription-based services, moving away from one-off device sales.
Software integrates devices into broader clinical workflows, increasing customer stickiness, improving efficiency, and enhancing overall outcomes, driving demand for connected solutions.

new_opportunities.description: Software, particularly SaMD, is unlocking innovative care models such as remote patient monitoring and data-driven decision support, extending healthcare value beyond traditional points of care and creating new market segments.
SaMD provides core clinical differentiation, improving patient outcomes (e.g., AI for polyp detection) and thus driving its adoption and market demand due to tangible clinical benefits.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of the structural shift in the medtech industry towards software, highlighting how Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) creates new revenue and care models. No explicit market size or CAGR provided, but significant new opportunities and demand drivers identified.
market_sizing.source_title: The future of delivering software as a medical device
